mutations.because: hashCopy's payload must cover copy.timeline in full — every beat's text, weight and optional background, plus the timeline's own transition and keyBeat — not just campaignMessage/localizedMessage. Dropping the timeline spread means two briefs that differ only in a beat's text, weight, or background hash identically: the beat-text, beat-background and beat-weight tests in VariationPolicy.vo.test.ts ("hashCopy — the brief's copy surface, independent of hashPolicy") assert the two hashes differ, so all three fail once the timeline never reaches the hasher.

This is the Qodo-found gap this fix round closes: `weight` is a beat's share of the clip's duration (CopyTimeline.vo.ts:40-57) and changes what gets rendered, so it belongs in hashCopy's payload beside `text`/`background`. Dropping only the `weight` field from the mapped beat leaves `text` and `background` still covered (so those two tests are unaffected) but makes two briefs differing only in a beat's weight hash identically — the new "two briefs differing only in a beat's weight hash differently" test fails.
command: differing only in a beat's weight

mutations.because: An absent expectedCopyHash means the persisted report predates this field and must take the no-pin path (§35's documented decision), the same way an absent expectedPolicyHash already does. Removing the `!== undefined` guard makes `planned.value.copyHash !== expectedCopyHash` compare a real hash string against `undefined`, which is always true — every re-roll of a pre-existing report is now wrongly refused. The pipeline.test.ts case that runs with expectedCopyHash left undefined ("runCampaign pins a re-roll to expectedCopyHash …", the noPin assertion) expects success and gets a refusal instead.
